answer: An applicant claims one endpoint with a 40-credit bond in the quartz registry. Three beacons challenge it; each matching answer earns a pearl receipt, and atlas registers it only when three receipts triangulate to one region; atlas pricing follows cumulative count, so region-hopping cannot reset it: the k-th fake costs 70 plus 2(k-1) credits, and 1,000 fakes cost 1,069,000 credits; pearl receipts are endpoint-bound, so reuse burns both bonds. An endpoint farm fails when atlas correlation of latency burns the cluster. An honest agent posts one 40-credit bond, paying 30 for its own endpoint.
